name: Fattoria Galardi Terra di Lavoro 2010
text:
## Fattoria Galardi Terra di Lavoro 2010

**The story.** Terra di Lavoro is one of the great modern wines of southern Italy, from vineyards on the slopes of the extinct [Roccamonfina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roccamonfina) volcano, in the commune of [Sessa Aurunca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sessa_Aurunca) in northern Campania ([see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Roccamonfina,+Caserta,+Italy&t=k)). In the 1990s a group of friends and relatives, none of them professional winemakers, set out to make a wine of the very highest level in an area never considered capable of one. Their consultant, Riccardo Cotarella, soon saw that the local pairing of [Aglianico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aglianico), for power and structure, and [Piedirosso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedirosso), for aroma and complexity, gave "magical results" on these hills. Italy's Finest Wines calls it a wine that redefined its whole area ([Italy's Finest Wines](https://www.italysfinestwines.it/galardi-2/), in Italian).

The name means "land of work", and was also the historical name of this area. Piedirosso, "red feet", is named for its red stalks, like a pigeon's feet; one of its local synonyms is Piede di Colombo, "dove's foot" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedirosso)).

**The vintage.** Jancis Robinson's vintage charts don't cover Campania. Antonio Galloni, though, had "a strong feeling the 2010 will occupy a place among the very finest vintages produced on this tiny vineyard".

**What the critics say for 2010.**
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate)** (Antonio Galloni, February 2013, as listed by [Farr Vintners](https://farrvintners.com/wine.php?wine=34500) and [Fine Wine Cellar](https://www.finewinecellar.co.uk/products/terra-di-lavoro-galardi-2010)). "An exotic melange of tar, smoke, graphite, blackberry jam and savory herbs explode from the glass"; intense and full-bodied, "yet also incredibly elegant. A big, breathtaking wine" that builds to "a deeply resonant, expressive finish". He would leave "this utterly beguiling Campanian red" alone for the better part of a decade. Anticipated maturity: 2020 to 2040. (Retailers list this note at 97+; the score itself wasn't on the pages I read.)
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.1** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is sixteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2040, matching Galloni's. So it is in its prime, with years to go. Aglianico is a tannic, long-lived grape, and at sixteen this should show tar, smoke, dried blackberry and herbs. Decant it two hours ahead.

**Serving and food.** Serve at 17 to 18°C. Campanian matches: slow-cooked Neapolitan [ragù](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neapolitan_rag%C3%B9), braised lamb, roast pork with fennel, or aged [Caciocavallo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caciocavallo).

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Terra di Lavoro. Older vintages turn up with merchants such as [Farr Vintners](https://farrvintners.com/wine.php?wine=34500) and at auction.

**From the history books**
- **An ancient settlement.** Around the Roccamonfina volcano are traces of Ausonian or Auruncan settlements, with polygonal walls from the 6th to 5th century BC ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roccamonfina)).
- **A royal possession.** In the Middle Ages the area was a fief of Neapolitan and papal noble families, and under the Bourbons a direct possession of the crown of the [Two Sicilies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Two_Sicilies) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roccamonfina)).

**Curious details**
- **The Devil's footprints.** On the volcano are fossil human footprints known as the [Ciampate del Diavolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciampate_del_Diavolo), "the Devil's tracks" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roccamonfina)).
- **Chestnut woods.** The town of Roccamonfina is surrounded by dense groves of sweet chestnut trees ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roccamonfina)).
